rules.statement: Build every absolute URL the server publishes (discovery endpoints, jwks_uri, registration_client_uri, verification_uri, check_session_iframe, interaction URLs) from the tenant's configured issuer base address, never from the incoming request's scheme, Host or path base.
rules.why: A request with a foreign Host otherwise yields a discovery document with the correct issuer but attacker-controlled endpoints, which makes it easy to steal client secrets and authorization codes.
rules.check: Look for URL generation that uses HttpContext/Request (e.g. LinkGenerator.GetUriByName(httpContext, ...), Request.Host, Request.Scheme, GetDisplayUrl) to produce URLs that are published to clients, instead of going through the tenant-issuer-anchored URL seam.

rules.statement: Derive the tenant's routing host from the host component of its issuer, and don't store a separate, independently settable host or domain value for routing.
rules.why: OIDC Discovery §4.3 requires the issuer to be identical to the URL the document was fetched from. A second writable copy can drift from it through ordinary administration.
rules.check: Flag new tenant properties, columns or settings holding a routing host/domain that can be set independently of the issuer, or routing that matches against anything other than the issuer-derived host.

rules.statement: Don't persist a second independently writable copy of a value that can be derived from another stored value; compute it on write into a column that is never set on its own.
rules.why: A second stored copy of a derivable value is a drift hazard no matter what guards it. Having one source of truth is the only guarantee of consistency.
rules.check: Look for entities or schemas that add a column duplicating derivable data, with setters, API fields or migrations that let it be written independently of its source.

rules.statement: Enforce tenant issuer uniqueness with a unique (filtered) database index on the normalized issuer.
rules.why: The issuer is the tenant's identity and is asserted in every token it mints, so a shared issuer makes two tenants' tokens indistinguishable to relying parties.
rules.check: Check that tenant schema or migration changes keep a unique index on the normalized issuer, and that issuers are normalized before they are stored or compared.

rules.statement: Don't put a unique schema constraint on the issuer-derived tenant host; enforce host uniqueness through validation only when host-based tenant resolution is in use.
rules.why: Path-based tenants legitimately share a host, so a unique host index would make the path strategy unusable beyond one tenant.
rules.check: Flag a unique index on the derived host column, or host-uniqueness checks applied regardless of the active tenant resolution strategy.

rules.statement: Model the tenant issuer as a first-class tenant property, not as a merged or inherited setting.
rules.why: A server-level issuer inherited by every tenant is meaningless. A value that has to opt out of the settings merge lattice is not a setting.
rules.check: Flag code that reads or writes the issuer through the settings/merge system (e.g. a tenant_issuer setting descriptor) instead of the tenant's own property.

rules.statement: Tests that assert on published URLs or Host-spoofing resistance must explicitly set a tenant issuer that differs from the request host.
rules.why: Without a pinned issuer, a test proving a spoofed Host cannot reach published URLs passes vacuously, because the request-derived value and the spoofed value are the same.
rules.check: Look for tests asserting discovery or endpoint URLs, or spoofed-Host behaviour, that don't configure an explicit issuer on the tenant.

rules.statement: When a migration replaces an independently stored value with a derived one, clear the old values instead of copying them into the new derived column.
rules.why: Copying keeps exactly the drift the change is meant to remove, such as rows that stay routable by a value they don't claim.
rules.check: Look for migrations that copy legacy column data into a new derived column instead of deriving it again from the source value or clearing it.
